files.rationale: Minimal literal question; each criterion states its interval condition and what belongs to the nearest neighbour instead.
Guideline-aware version; the instructions carry the special event rules, and the criteria say how those rules map to options.
Timeline framing; each option is described by where the start and end points of the events fall, with contrasts to the nearest neighbour.

Coarse-to-fine hierarchy; first decide whether a relation is stated or clearly implied (else VAGUE), then choose between ordering (non-overlapping) and overlap, then pick the fine relation, with contrastive criteria at each step.
One-vs-rest; each label is judged as an independent true/false statement about the writer's intended relation, and the most probable label wins.
Branch cascade; a VAGUE gate, then an overlap gate, then flat choices whose criteria contrast each option with its nearest neighbour.

writer_input: task/label definitions and the paper seed program; no data examples, no gold labels
